## Correctness review

### Regex boundaries

The `_HF_CITED_RE` alt-family `issue\d+_[\w\-]+` requires DIGITS immediately after `issue` (no separator), while a repo-relative git path is `issue_<N>/` (underscore between `issue` and digits). The regex naturally discriminates — `issue_1434/results.jsonl` fails the `\d` at position 5 and cannot match. Test 5 (`test_issue_underscore_git_path_not_matched_by_hf_regex`) pins this — `vci.extract_hf_cited_basenames("Reads eval_results/issue_1434/results.jsonl for phase 2.") == set()`.

The anchored-segments form `(?:/[\w.\-]+)*/(?P<name>...)` prevents the greedy-backtrack failure the earlier `[\w./\-]*` had (truncating `pool.jsonl` → `l.jsonl`). Segments are alphanumeric + underscore + dot + dash, which covers HF repo path components.

Regex composition (`re.compile(...)` with string concatenation of `_BARE_EXTS`) produces well-formed anchored patterns. ✓

### Refactor behavior preservation

All three `findings.append(...)` calls inside the Channel-B per-path loop moved to `pending.append(...)`:
- deduped-channel-a branch (`if path in a_paths`)
- bare-name-declared-output skip branch (declared under `outputs:`)
- classify()/full ladder branch (the #1434 protection surface)

Each `continue` still exits the per-path loop iteration correctly. The `bare-name-unresolved` skip stays on `findings.append` (correctly outside the per-path loop). The `foreign` list and the trailing `bare-name-foreign-issue` warning are unchanged and orthogonal to `pending`. `findings.extend(pending)` at the end of the per-name block promotes the pending list into `findings` after downgrade. ✓

### #1434 protection

The downgrade only fires when `name in hf_cited OR in_ref_paths`. If neither evidence branch fires, `pending` is unmodified and every `untracked-local-only` FAIL survives into `findings`. Test 4 (`test_bare_name_untracked_still_fails_when_no_hf_citation_and_single_resolution`) pins this — an untracked-local-only citation with NO HF citation and single resolution → `_main` returns 1. ✓

### Precedence

`if name in hf_cited: ... elif in_ref_paths: ...` — `hf-staged` wins when both apply. Matches plan v2's stated precedence. ✓

### Mutation safety

`for i, f in enumerate(pending):` + `pending[i] = Finding(...)` — Python list-index assignment is safe during `enumerate` iteration (iterator holds the list reference, not the elements). Iteration order preserved. ✓

### Multi-path downgrade under one `name`

If `hf_cited` contains a basename that resolves to MULTIPLE untracked local paths, all get downgraded to `hf-staged` WARNs — correct, all are coincidental VM mirrors of the same HF-staged file. ✓
